- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for such periods.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.5 to -0.5 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment volatility; for 30-day forecasts, smooth sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days to dampen noise.
- When true price rises >5% from prior period, model often lags by 1–3 days; shift forecast up by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.4), model undercorrects; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast 2–3 days ahead.
